dimensions.assessment: Affects online video game providers, minor users, their parents or legal guardians, the Federal Trade Commission, and state attorneys general nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: An online video game provider shall provide safeguards to the parent of a covered user of an interactive online video game

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory software and default setting changes on video game companies, backed by federal trade regulation enforcement and state civil lawsuits.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of subsection (b) shall be treated as a violation of a regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act

dimensions.assessment: Implies administrative enforcement costs for the FTC and state agencies, but does not provide specific funding amounts or appropriations.
Creates a new national regulatory standard for interactive online video games, grants enforcement powers to the FTC and states, and preempts state laws.
dimensions.evidence: No State or political subdivision of a State may prescribe, maintain, or enforce any law... if such law... relates to the provisions of this Act.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent ongoing operational requirements on online video game providers taking effect one year after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This subsection shall take effect on the date that is 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific estimates of administrative or compliance expenses for video game providers and regulatory agencies.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires online video game providers to implement default parent-controlled communication safeguards for minors under 18, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, while preempting state-level laws on the subject.

summary: The Safer Guarding of Adolescents from Malicious Interactions on Network Games Act (Safer GAMING Act) requires online video game providers to give parents safeguards to limit communication between minor users and other users. These safeguards must be accessible, easy to use, enabled by default for minors, and only disableable by a parent. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general are authorized to enforce these requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Have communication safeguards enabled by default on their interactive online video game accounts.
Receive safeguards allowing them to limit communication between minor users and other users, with the sole ability to disable those safeguards.
affected_groups.group: Parents or legal guardians of minors

affected_groups.effect: Must provide required communication safeguards, ensure they are enabled by default and parent-controlled, and face enforcement actions by the FTC or state officials for non-compliance.
Empowered to enforce the safeguard requirements, investigate, seek penalties, and bring civil actions against violators.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Requires interactive online video game providers to give parents safeguards to limit communication between minor users and any other users.
Mandates that communication safeguards are accessible, easy to use, enabled by default on minor accounts, and disableable only by a parent.
Applies the most protective level of privacy and safety settings by default for minors, which can only be disabled by their parents.
Sets the effective date for the safeguard requirements to one year after the date of enactment.
Treats violations of the safeguard requirements as violations of regulations regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.
Allows state attorneys general, officials, or agencies to bring civil actions in state or federal court on behalf of state residents for violations.
Preempts any state or local laws, rules, regulations, or requirements related to the provisions of this Act.
missing_information: Specific penalties or fine amounts for violating the Act.
Detailed methods or technical standards required for verifying user ages or parental status.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Safer Guarding of Adolescents from Malicious Interactions on Network Games Act (Safer GAMING Act) requires online video game providers to give parents safeguards to limit communication between minor users and other users. These safeguards must be accessible, easy to use, enabled by default for minors, and only disableable by a parent. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general are authorized to enforce these requirements.
summary_detail.significance: The Safer GAMING Act establishes federal mandates for interactive online video games regarding minor safety and parent communication controls. It gives enforcement authority to both the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general while preempting state-level laws on the same subject.
